lens: The map: what Ren asked for, what each existing picture's nodes and edges are, what graph the atlas data already holds, and what map to build first.
in_one_paragraph: Ren asked on 4 November for "all attractors, phase transitions" mapped, and on 6 November whether "we can see how they are connected together". The two requests produced two artefacts, both called a map, and neither draws attractors and the transitions among them. The connection map (map.html, "the loom") has documents as nodes: 16 earlier folders, 12 domains, and the account's chapters. The terrain has 8 family boxes joined by arrows that carry counts. The theory graph is a dependency graph of files, proofs and modules. The lineage is a timeline. Measured on dynamics.json, the dynamics themselves barely connect: 70 of 321 exits name another dynamic, giving 62 distinct edges that touch 73 of 183 nodes. 110 dynamics are isolated, the longest route is 3 steps, and closed capture (the meta-attractor's closed form) has no edge in or out. The other 251 exits end in "a state in words": 247 distinct sentences of about 186 characters, so the places a course ends up (ended, locked, kept, cycling, unlocked, giving, withholding) are never nodes. The atlas's unit is a proved record's mechanism, which is a law and not a place. A layer of some 30 to 40 regimes is missing between the 8 families and the 183 dynamics. Most of the content for it exists already: 321 exits with law, strength and dropped premise; 103 transitions with kind and a from/to in words; 212 tradition and field entries that reach 129 dynamics through records. What must be made is the regime list, the assignment of about 450 sentences to it, and plain labels. I would build one regime map first: places where something forms, persists or ends, arrows for how it changes, laid out on fixed coordinates, with the traditions' names as an overlay.

findings.what: What Ren asked for, in his words. He asked for attractors and phase transitions as the things mapped, and for the traditions to sit at places on that map. The word 'topology' first appears on 11 November; a search of the conversations from 4 November on finds no earlier use.
findings.quote: "please eventually map out all attractors, phase transitions, what maps onto existing wisdoms, systems thinking, philosophy, cultures and scientific/logic understanding" (11-04). "a full, very detailed, structured, well thought, data collection, that can be visualized in all different ways" (11-04). "哲学中的各种理论 例如对立统一，是不是也可以在地图的一些位置找到？" (11-10). "we need to make dynamics connected, mapped, and 'unified'" (11-10). "它可以用什么更好的数据结构来visualize？存储？索引？理解？" (11-09).
findings.why_it_matters: The request was specific from the first day: nodes are attractors, edges are transitions, and traditions have positions (位置). No existing picture has those nodes and edges.

findings.what: How 'map' came to mean 'connection map'. On 6 November Ren asked whether the theories and wisdoms are interconnected. The session offered 'a crosswalk ... and a viewable map', and he said to build it. That became map.html. So the 6 November question got a picture of connections between documents, and the 4 November request got a data collection with no picture until terrain.svg on 10 November.
findings.quote: "The connection map: one page that shows how the earlier folders and the domains of thought meet the live account"
findings.why_it_matters: His phrase 'connections between different components' is literally accurate. The components are folders and chapters.

findings.what: The connection map's nodes are documents. On the site it is 'The loom': the left column is the author's own 16 earlier folders, the centre beam is the account's pages (The one page, The overview, 01 The root, 02 ...), and the right column is 12 domains of thought. A thread is one AI reading of a claim against a chapter section. Of 1,183 entries, 838 are 'earlier-folders' and 345 are traditions and fields.
findings.quote: "EARLIER FOLDERS · THE LIVE ACCOUNT · DOMAINS OF THOUGHT"; "A row is an earlier folder or a domain of thought, a column the part of the account its claims are read against"
findings.why_it_matters: A reader learns that Buddhist thought has 10 readings against chapter 7. They do not learn where 無明 or the tragedy of the commons sits among the dynamics. 71% of the threads are the project's own earlier folders, so the picture is mostly the work connecting to itself.

findings.what: The terrain picture has 8 nodes, and its arrows are counts. It draws 55 cross-family exits (47 a law places, 8 no law shows). The other 266 of 321 exits appear only as numbers inside the boxes. Box positions carry no meaning; the boxes sit on a ring in letter order.
findings.where: /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/atlas/terrain.svg, shown in README.md line 25, ONE-PAGE.md line 36, ATLAS.md, THEORY-GRAPH.md and TERRAIN.md
findings.quote: "A. Absorption and ending · 29 dynamics · read · 2 exits within · 35 to a state in words"; caption: "an arrow counts recorded exits between two families, not a route"
findings.why_it_matters: This is the first picture after the README says 'A map of how anything forms, lasts, changes and ends'. From it a reader cannot find the meta-attractor, a way into it, or a way out. 'read' and 'a state in words' are the project's bookkeeping terms. The picture shows how complete the data entry is, not the dynamics. Its caption then tells the reader it is not a route.

findings.what: The per-family exit diagrams are not drawn on the reader's site. TERRAIN.md holds 8 mermaid flowcharts. The site shows them as collapsed text with a note, followed by tables. The page is about 22,800 words and 53,000 pixels tall.
findings.quote: "A diagram GitHub draws from the text below; the site shows the text. See it drawn on GitHub."
findings.why_it_matters: On the public site the only drawn picture of the dynamics is the 8-box count picture. Where the flowcharts do render (GitHub), each word-state is an oval of truncated theorem text, e.g. 'outside the region R at step n + 1 from inside it at step n: the move…'.

findings.what: The theory graph and spine picture map the artefact, not the dynamics. The data has 3,287 nodes (1,724 corpus texts, 556 sections, 539 theorems, 400 Lean modules, 41 concepts) and 7,167 edges (proved-in, related, formal-reuse, imports, states). spine.svg draws 8 chapter circles around 'The grammar', with curves counting citations between chapters. standings.svg draws 117 squares by derivation class. lineage.svg is a timeline of 50 events.
findings.quote: "The eight chapters and their recorded uses of one another"; "An edge records a dependence, a citation or a registered reading, not an agreement in meaning"
findings.why_it_matters: Every picture a reader reaches has chapters, folders, families, declarations or dates as nodes. None has a place a course can be in. Chapter 2, whose file is named 02-MAP and which defines the regions 生成 / 守 / 退化, contains no image. None of chapters 01 to 08 does.

findings.what: The exit graph among dynamics is nearly empty. 70 of 321 exits name a dynamic, giving 62 distinct directed edges. 73 of 183 dynamics are touched and 110 are isolated. The weakly connected components are one of 17, two of 5, four of 3 and seventeen pairs. The longest route is 3 steps. There are 5 small cycles (four 2-cycles and one 3-cycle). 56 dynamics have no exit at all. 17 of the 70 dynamic-to-dynamic exits join laws stated on different bases.
findings.quote: Longest route: "Readings carried along a line…" → "Selection blind beyond the coupling closure" → "Reading in time…" → "The point of no return of a regime"
findings.why_it_matters: There is no topology to show at this grain, however it is drawn. The one 17-node component is the recent K-train work (readings, pools, the lock drawing its readers out). The rest of the atlas is islands.

findings.what: The meta-attractor is an isolated node. closed-capture has in-degree 0 and out-degree 0 among dynamics; its 2 exits end in sentences. capture-through-the-rule is the same. The wide meta-attractor and the second and third orders of capture have no record, no exits and no transitions.
findings.where: /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/atlas/entries/dynamics.json: ids closed-capture, capture-through-the-rule, self-reproducing-selection-across-carriers (standing 'open'), capture-reaching-the-routes-of-correction and selection-for-narrowing-what-couples-in (standing 'reading'); /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/atlas/families/c.md
findings.quote: "To a state, in words: 'at the step after every reading step r with N ≤ b + r, the rule in force does not favour, so the course is not locked there, whatever the share'"
findings.why_it_matters: The README's first paragraph is about this loop, yet the map has no edge saying how a course gets into it or where its exits lead. The content exists as prose: `ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss` drops the premise Unread, `readers_uniform_locks` is a way in, and there are critical-mass and deadline laws. None of it is a graph edge, because the destination 'not locked' is not a node.

findings.what: The places are sentences. 251 of 321 exits end in 'a state in words'. These are 247 distinct sentences with a median of 186 characters; 56 begin 'a witness'. 96 transitions give from and to in words (95 and 94 distinct). None resolves to a shared id. A keyword pass puts 199 of the 251 into nine recurring kinds: ended or level 0 (69), persists or kept (54), giving or withholding (48), locked or stays (45), restored or renewed (40), rise or widening (39), pool or reader or selection (24), unread or alike (13), cycle (8). A sentence can hit several kinds.
findings.quote: JOINS.md: "Exits that name a destination (a dynamic, or a state in words) that a law shows | 307 of 321"
findings.why_it_matters: The attractors are in the data, but as non-repeating theorem conclusions. The 9 November joint reading asked for each exit to end at a 'destination predicate' (去处谓词). What was built is free text, so no two exits can meet at one place. The JOINS measure counts a 186-character sentence as a named destination. That is how the count went from 22 of 285 to 307 of 321 while the topology stayed absent, the same kind of measure failure as the rubric.

findings.what: The atlas's unit mixes kinds of thing. Some dynamics are regimes ('Closed capture', 'The rest theorem'). Some are boundaries ('The point of no return of a regime', 'The exit from a margin'). Some are general laws about all transitions ('Every loss passes a juncture'). Some are remedies ('A coupling for each step kept', 'Division by exclusive footprints'). One is a list of edges ('Four routes of transition, none a proved phase transition'). So an exit edge means different things. The 4 edges from 'A rule rebuilt from the members it limits' to 'The ends of a rule rebuilt from its members' are one record split in two. The 9 B→H edges are 'under this changed coupling the drain becomes a kept region'.
findings.quote: B→H: "Reward each step a need stays met: where the coupling covers the renewal forgone a step and exceeds the end, every optimum keeps the dependence at every horizon."
findings.why_it_matters: 'A dynamic' is roughly one proved record's mechanism. That is the right unit for a catalogue and the wrong node for a map a person reads. On a map, regimes are places, boundaries and remedies are arrows, and laws are what stands behind both. The B→H remedy edges are some of the most valuable alignment content in the atlas, and on the terrain they are the numeral '9'.

findings.what: No dynamic has a label a person can read at a glance, and none carries a name a tradition gives it. Names are theorem titles in the work's vocabulary: median 43 characters, 47 over 60. Mechanisms have a median of 182 words, 33,033 in total. There is no short-label, plain-gloss or example field. 183 names are in English and 6 in Chinese.
findings.quote: "Readings carried along a line, told apart by its standing late only within its coupling closure"; "Own count misses joint excess"
findings.why_it_matters: 'Own count misses joint excess' is what Hardin, Aristotle and Thucydides, Parfit and Roman law are each read against in the crosswalk, 7 tradition entries in all, and the node does not say 'tragedy of the commons'. A reader cannot recognise on the map what they already know. This is where 'our vocabulary so much' bites hardest.

findings.what: The wisdom layer can already be attached to dynamics, and no picture does it. Correspondence targets point at 579 chapter anchors. Through records, 1,414 of 3,772 targets resolve to a dynamic. 212 of the 345 tradition and field entries reach 129 of 183 dynamics. Closed capture carries 24 (Goodhart, Stigler-type capture, Plato's cave, Ibn Khaldun, Acemoglu and Robinson, ...). The point of no return carries 10 (alternative stable states, Allee effects, the saddle-node, 从善如登，从恶如崩).
findings.quote: "Tragedy of the commons as a trap of missing feedback"; "Alternative stable states"; "Stigler: regulation acquired by the regulated"; "Value lock-in"
findings.why_it_matters: This is the 'map of wisdom' Ren describes: one place, many traditions' names for it, each marked agreement, scope or divergence. The data join exists. The loom draws it against chapters instead. Caveat: 327 of the 345 rest on AI knowledge of texts not stored, and the page's own check estimates 14.2% wrong labels.

findings.what: The other edge kinds do not give a readable topology either. Shared premises: 1,669 premises, 1,632 of them 'hypothesis of a law'; 1,297 are used by one dynamic only. With the hubs included, 151 dynamics form one component only because everything shares 'natural-number amounts' (56), 'balance' (41) and 'decided' (36). Case-of: 104 general laws, 66 dynamics are cases, and only 44 of the general laws sit in any dynamic. Shared declarations: 42 pairs. Dropped premises: 191 distinct across 307 exits, 146 dropped once; 'Unread' is dropped 5 times. Compositions: 10. Situations: 1. Tests bound: 22 tests on 16 dynamics.
findings.where: /Users/ren/theories/theories/becoming/results/atlas/entries/premises.json, dynamics.json (premises[].takes, case_of, drops, compose), situations.json, bindings.json
findings.quote: "card-natural-number-amounts: a positive amount is at least one unit" (used by 56 dynamics)
findings.why_it_matters: The premise ledger is at Lean-hypothesis grain. It is honest and checkable, and too fine to act as the levers of a map. The joint reading predicted that exits of families C and D would converge on 'reads beyond the share'. The data cannot show that until dropped premises are also grouped into a few dozen named levers.

findings.what: 'Map' names at least five different things in the public face: the work itself; MAP.md, a guide to the repository's files; chapter 02-MAP, the formal regions; map.html, the loom; and the terrain and atlas. The nav's 'See' group lists Atlas, Graph, Connections, How it grew, Glossary and Where everything is, with no item called the map.
findings.quote: README: "A map of how anything forms, lasts, changes and ends"; MAP.md: "# Where everything is ... A guide for visitors"
findings.why_it_matters: A reader told 'this is a map' who looks for the map finds a file guide, a formal chapter, a loom of folders and an 8-box count diagram. There is no single thing to point at.

findings.what: The atlas has no Chinese edition and its vocabulary is closed in English. The Chinese nav links 图集（英文） and 连接图（英文）. Only CROSSWALK.zh.md and connections.zh.svg exist beside the atlas pages.
findings.why_it_matters: Ren's stated order for signifiers is 文言 first, then English. A regime layer of about 36 names is small enough to name in three registers, which the 183 theorem titles are not.

proposals.change: Build first: one regime map. Places are where something forms, persists or ends; arrows are how it changes. About 36 regimes sit between the 8 families and the 183 dynamics, on fixed coordinates.
proposals.how:
Add entries/regimes.json with about 36 entries. Each has: id; a label of at most 4 words (en, zh, 文言 where a chapter gives one); a one-sentence plain gloss; one everyday example; sector (forms, persists or ends); ring (1 a thing and what sustains it, 2 several drawing or giving together, 3 a selection and what it reads, 4 a selection that forms its own rule or readers); a hand-set slot so places never move between renders; how far seen.

Add `to_regime` to each of the 251 word-exits and `from_regime`/`to_regime` to the 96 transitions, or `unresolved` with a reason. Add `at` (the regimes its laws of staying hold in) to each dynamic.

A generator beside tools/research/atlas.py writes a static SVG for the README and one HTML page with inline SVG and a small script. Line style is exact, sufficient, necessary, witness, or no law. Clicking a place opens a panel with the gloss, example, names traditions give it, laws of staying (links into families/*.md), ways in, ways out with condition and lever, tests and what is open. Clicking an arrow gives the condition, kind, strength, dropped premise, Lean law, base and source. Zoom 0 is the 12 cells with 6 to 8 landmark places. Zoom 1 is all the regimes. Zoom 2 is the existing entry pages, unchanged.

Pilot on family C, family E and the stock threshold (margin-of-a-regime) before resolving all 450 sentences. Put it first on the home page under the opening sentence, call it 'the map' in the nav, and rename map.html 'the loom' or 'connections'.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: A drawn arrow between places reads as 'courses go there'. The data says exits do not compose, 160 of 321 are witnesses, and 17 of 70 named exits cross bases. So every arrow has to carry its strength visibly, and the picture needs a filter for 'only what a law shows on one model'. Sector and ring are a reading assigned by hand; chapter 02 itself says "§§4–9 are not read as regions", so the sectors must not be labelled 生成/守/退化 as if proved. Resolving sentences to regimes is AI curation and will have errors. Show the unresolved count on the map and have two independent assignments with the disagreements listed. The map will also show honestly that the wide meta-attractor is an outline with no edges.

proposals.change: Second: the same map with the traditions' names on it, as the wisdom overlay. It replaces the loom's chapter beam with places.
proposals.how: Roll up correspondences.json through targets[].record to dynamics and then to regimes. That is 212 of 345 tradition and field entries today. In the regime map add a 'names' switch per domain (systems thinking, ecology, economics, Chinese classical, Buddhist, ...). Each place lists the entries read against it, with relation (agreement 相合, scope 定域, divergence 相分, contrary reading 反读) and source basis. Searching 'tragedy of the commons', 'Goodhart' or '一治一乱' flies to its place. Entries that reach no place are listed in a margin as 'not on the map yet'; that is 133 of 345 plus the 105 not carried. Keep the loom as a secondary view for the earlier folders.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: 327 of the 345 rest on AI knowledge of a text not stored, with an estimated 14.2% wrong labels. Putting familiar names on nodes lends borrowed authority, and a reader will take 'Goodhart' on a node as 'this is Goodhart's law' when the entry says 'scope'. The relation has to show on the label itself. It also loses the loom's chapter-level reading, which some reviewers use.

proposals.change: Third: exact small pictures of single dynamics, phase portraits and paired courses. Each is a theorem drawn, placed on the regime's panel and on the one page.
proposals.how: (a) Paired courses for 'a selection blind beyond what it reads' and for closed capture: two courses identical in every coordinate the selection reads (share, rule) and diverging in the unread one (loss), drawn from the Lean models' own step functions. (b) Phase portraits where the law is an exact threshold: the stock's point of no return (`RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below`, start below H + y), the level × recent-giving plane (threshold-in-the-state-plane), capture's critical mass (`DrawnShaping.critical_mass_iff`, lo < c < hi) with the deadline for reading the loss (`ReadInTime.deadline`), and waiting tolerance. Evaluate on a grid and spot-check sample cells against Lean `decide`. Five or six pictures, each a small static SVG from a script. The 9 November joint reading already proposed both (§2.4, pictures 2 and 3); neither was built.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: A Python re-implementation of a Lean model can drift from the Lean, so each picture must be checked at sample points. A model's phase portrait may be taken for the world's; each needs the base on its face ('on a named model'). These pictures show dynamics well but give no topology on their own, which is why they come after the regime map. The paired-courses picture alone could go on the home page before anything else is built.

proposals.change: Supporting data change: group the dropped premises into a few dozen named levers.
proposals.how: Add a `lever` id to each premise an exit drops. There are 191 distinct across 307 exits, 146 dropped once. Example: 'read what lies beyond the share' would cover closedcapture-unread and its kin. Arrows can then be coloured or filtered by lever, and the premise × regime matrix the joint reading wanted (which lever opens which locks) can be computed.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: Grouping Lean hypotheses under a plain name loses exactness. Keep the Lean premise one click below the lever, and never state a law at lever grain.

demonstration:
SPEC OF THE FIRST MAP ("the map": forms, persists, ends; arrows are changes)

1. NODE = a regime. A regime is a condition a course can be in for a stretch or for good, said as a plain predicate. About 36 in all, in a new file theories/becoming/results/atlas/entries/regimes.json.
Fields: id; label {en, zh, wenyan?} of at most 4 words; gloss, one sentence with no project vocabulary; example, one everyday case; sector ∈ {forms, persists, ends}; ring ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}; slot, an integer set by hand; held_by, the dynamic ids whose laws say a course stays; known_as, computed from correspondences; how_far ∈ {law on any process, law on World, law on a named model, argued, reading, open}; valence, always "none asserted".

Example nodes. Ids are new; the sources are existing dynamics:
- kept-above-the-point (ring 1, persists). "A renewed stock above its point of no return." From margin-of-a-regime: "from H + y up to hi it never ends". Known as: alternative stable states, Allee effects, saddle-node.
- ended-for-good (ring 1, ends). "Ended, and does not come back." From loss-of-renewal-for-good, attraction-is-not-returning, what-a-gate-keeps ("an empty pool stays empty").
- settles-in-a-band (ring 1, persists) and cycles-without-end (ring 1, persists). From two-sided-regulation-and-late-reading, overshooting-thermostat-alternates, and "Beyond the gap an opposing exchange crosses and can oscillate for ever".
- at-rest (ring 1, persists). From "The rest theorem".
- widening (ring 1, forms). From "Where the possible grows": "the possible under Q keeps widening along the course".
- commons-drained (ring 2, ends). "Each within its own count, together beyond what is given." From own-count-misses-joint-excess. Known as: Hardin, Aristotle and Thucydides, Parfit.
- commons-kept (ring 2, persists). "The joint take stays within what is given." Destination of that dynamic's exit: "the level of c never falls below its start". Also division-by-exclusive-footprints.
- mutual-giving and total-withholding (ring 2, persists). From giving-that-waits-on-giving and restoring-giving-from-the-worst-start.
- blind-drain (ring 3, persists and ends). "Meets its measure while what it does not read is lost." From unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure. Known as: Goodhart (scope), Plato's cave, evolutionary traps.
- closed-lock (ring 4, persists). "Rule and its reading both formed from the share it selects; stays locked while the unread loss grows." From closed-capture (`ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss`). 24 tradition entries.
- not-locked (ring 4). "The rule in force no longer favours its winners." Destination of both closed-capture exits.
- lock-without-readers (ring 4, persists). From the-lock-draws-its-readers-out.
- wide-meta-attractor (ring 4). A dotted outline with no arrows. From self-reproducing-selection-across-carriers, standing "open".

2. EDGE = a change from one regime to another. Edges are computed from exits[] and transitions[] once each end carries a regime id.
Fields: from; to; condition, in plain words; kind, one of vocabulary.json's 11 (exact threshold, tipping in a parameter, window or deadline, critical mass, pace bound, exit by drift, loop onset, juncture, ...); strength ∈ {exact, sufficient, necessary, witness} or standing ∈ {argued, conjectured, reading, open}; lever, the premise dropped; law, the Lean name; base; via, the dynamic id; tests.

Examples, all from the data:
- kept-above-the-point ⇄ ended-for-good. Exact threshold. `Becoming.RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below`: "a level up to hi ends exactly where it starts below H + y". Base: a named model. Tests: margin-measured (run).
- commons-drained → commons-kept. Sufficient. `Becoming.Flow.joint_keeps`, lever flow-joint-excess. Also `Becoming.Flow.level_kept_of_plans` (division by exclusive footprints).
- closed-lock → not-locked. Sufficient. `Becoming.ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss`, lever Unread: "Read what lies beyond the share".
- any start → closed-lock. Pace bound. `Becoming.ClosedCapture.readers_uniform_locks`: "every course is locked from the step after its second reading step".
- closed-lock ⇄ locked-the-other-way. Critical mass, `Becoming.DrawnShaping.critical_mass_iff` (lo < c < hi). Window or deadline, `Becoming.ReadInTime.deadline`.
- settles-in-a-band → cycles-without-end, sufficient. settles-in-a-band → ended-for-good, sufficient: "a level below m at T never returns to m". Both via two-sided-regulation-and-late-reading.
- total-withholding → mutual-giving. Sufficient, `Becoming.Withholding.gives_without_chain`, lever withholding-chain. Witness, `Becoming.Withholding.Ring.givesFirst_restores`.
- blind-drain → lock-without-readers. No law, standing "reading". Drawn dashed.

3. LAYOUT. A wheel on fixed polar coordinates with no force layout, so places never move.
- Three 120° sectors labelled FORMS, PERSISTS and ENDS. Legend line: "Places: where something forms, persists or ends. Arrows: how it changes."
- Four rings from the centre out: a thing and what sustains it; several together; a selection and what it reads; a selection that forms its own rule or readers.
- A node sits at (sector, ring, slot). A wheel is used so that no sector is "up".
- Line style: thick solid for exact; solid for sufficient; thin with an open head for necessary ("leaving requires"); dotted for witness (one constructed course); dashed amber for no law. One ink colour, no red or green.
- A corner note gives the counts drawn and the count unresolved. The legend says sector and ring are a reading assigned by hand.

4. LAYERS.
- Zoom 0: 12 cells, about 8 landmark places and the thickest arrows. This is the README picture.
- Zoom 1: all regimes and arrows.
- Click a place: a panel with the gloss, example, names traditions give it with their relation, laws of staying (links to the families/*.md sections), ways in, ways out, tests and what is open.
- Click an arrow: condition, kind, strength, lever, law, base, source.
- Filters: only what a law shows; one ring; has a test; a domain's names.

5. FROM EXISTING DATA. Law, strength, drops, edge text and source for 321 exits. Kind, condition and declarations for 103 transitions. compose (10). tests and bindings. known_as, through records. Family and base.

6. MUST BE MADE.
- regimes.json, about 36 entries.
- Regime ids on 251 exit sentences and 96 × 2 transition ends, or "unresolved". Do two independent passes and list the disagreements.
- `at` on the 183 dynamics.
- Chinese labels.
- Pilot scope: family C (17 dynamics, 25 word-exits, 18 transitions), family E (10) and margin-of-a-regime.
where_ren_may_be_wrong_or_incomplete:
1. "I don't think we have something like a map." No picture is one. The data is much closer than the pictures suggest: 321 exits each with a law, a strength and a dropped premise; 103 transitions with kinds and both ends; 212 tradition entries already joinable to 129 dynamics. What is missing is one curated layer (about 36 regimes and about 450 sentence assignments) and plain labels. That is days of work on top of the atlas, not a restart. Throwing the atlas away for a hand-drawn concept map would lose the thing that makes this map checkable.

2. A map with real topology will claim more than is proved unless it is drawn carefully. Half of all exits (160 of 321) are witnesses, meaning one constructed course. The TERRAIN page says exits do not compose ("without checking that one exit's destination meets the next exit's conditions"). 17 of 70 named exits join laws on different models. The atlas itself has an entry titled "Four routes of transition, none a proved phase transition". The terrain's dullness comes from guarding against this with captions and counts. That kept the accuracy and lost the reader. If "make it a map" is followed naively, the result is the opposite failure: a persuasive diagram of routes nobody has shown. The fix is to put strength into the line style and offer a "law-only" filter. Hiding the limits, or hiding the picture, both fail.

3. "Something more like a Wikipedia." The per-entry pages already exist in effect as sections of families/*.md. What they lack is a lead sentence in plain words, a known name, an example and a view of their neighbours. A wiki of 183 pages without a top map would reproduce the present experience of many pages with no shape. The index he wants is the map; the wiki pages hang from it.

4. On dualism. The atlas already does the non-dual thing as data: `valence: "none asserted"` on all 183, and 'exit' is used alike for leaving a lock and for losing a kept region. But the words that carry the map are valenced in ordinary English: drain, capture, lock, stagnation, degeneration, exit. A reader will read the picture as bad places and escapes. A layout with endings at the bottom would add to that, which is why I propose a wheel. Renaming is not free either. 'Lock' and 'drain' are also the words a newcomer understands at once, and replacing them with neutral coinages would increase the 'our vocabulary' problem he also names. The two complaints pull against each other here, and he should decide which gives.
